simple.meaning: אָבָק (ʼâbâq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “light particles (as volatile ).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across Exodus, Deuteronomy, Isaiah, Ezekiel, Nahum, beginning at Exodus 9:9. Its contexts include family line, kingship, city, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָבָק (H80).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.full: H80. abaq אָבָק noun masculine Ezek 26:10 dust — ׳א Deut 28:24 3 t.; construct אֲבַק Nahum 1:3 ; suffix אֲבָקָם Ezek 26:10 — dust (? fleeing, flying; synonym עָפָר = often dust lying on or composing ground) Exod 9:9 ; Ezek 26:10 ; Deut 28:24 (|| עָפָר ) Isa 5:24 (|| מָק ) 29:5 (|| מֹץ ); figurative of clouds under Yahweh's feet Nahum 1:3 .

occurrences.englishText: It shall become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boils and blisters breaking out on man and on animal, throughout all the land of Egypt.”
Yahweh will make the rain of your land powder and dust. It will come down on you from the sky, until you are destroyed.
Therefore as the tongue of fire devours the stubble,
But the multitude of your foes will be like fine dust, and the multitude of the ruthless ones like chaff that blows away. Yes, it will be in an instant, suddenly.

By reason of the abundance of his horses, their dust will cover you. Your walls will shake at the noise of the horsemen, of the wagons, and of the chariots, when he enters into your gates, as men enter into a city which is broken open.
Yahweh is slow to anger, and great in power, and will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. Yahweh has his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
